newsitem.title: USA: Kansas winter wheat condition improves slightly.
newsitem.headline: Kansas winter wheat condition improves slightly.

text.p: The Kansas winter wheat crop showed slight improvement during the week ended Sunday, the state's agricultural statistics service said Monday in its weekly crop weather report.
A slightly larger percentage of the crop was recorded as good to excellent this week, as the crop continued breaking dormancy, the report said.
Wheat condition was rated 20 percent excellent, 64 good, 13 fair and three poor. That compared to last week's rating of 24 percent excellent, 58 percent good, 16 percent fair and two percent poor.
As of Sunday, six percent of the crop was jointing, compared with nil last year and the five-year average of four percent.

Insect and disease infestations remain minimal, with a few reports of armyworms, brown wheat mites and various types of mosaic in isolated areas. Rust did survive the winter in the southern tier of counties, but damage remains minimal.
Seeding of oats advanced to 52 percent complete, behind 64 percent last year but on par with the average of 53 percent.
Topsoil moisture was rated 11 percent short to very short, 80 adequate and nine surplus.
